new.title: The zero-key prefix contributes an exact power of two to masked suffix transcript counts
new.statement:
∀ (k d a h start init last c q : Nat), 0 < d → 0 < h → h ≤ a → a+2+2*d ≤ k →
  ∀ (key : Finset Nat → Fin q → Nat) (sensors : Finset Nat → Fin q → Finset Nat),
  let words := Finset.range (2^k)
  let rot := fun (s z : Nat) => ((z <<< (s % k)) ||| (z >>> (k - s % k))) % 2^k
  let mix := fun z : Nat => z ^^^ rot d z ^^^ rot (k-d) z
  let label := fun (u x j : Nat) =>
    let y := mix (rot init (x % 2^k) ^^^ u)
    let atSite := fun i : Nat => (start+i) % k
    xor (xor (y.testBit (atSite j))
      (!(y.testBit (atSite (j+1))) && y.testBit (atSite (j+2))))
      (xor ((rot last (x % 2^k)).testBit (atSite j)) (c.testBit (atSite j)))
  let block := fun (u x offset len : Nat) =>
    (Finset.range len).filter (fun i => label u x (offset+i))
  let extras := fun u : Nat =>
    let y := block u 0 (a-h) h
    fun j : Fin q => (block u (key y j) (a-h) h) ∩ sensors y j
  let transcripts := fun (offset len : Nat) =>
    words.image (fun u => (block u 0 offset len, extras u))
  (transcripts 0 a).card = 2^(a-h) * (transcripts (a-h) h).card
new.unlocks: reduces sparse key and sensor design to a suffix at every admissible width
new.context: Unwrap the a+2 mixed sites. In increasing order solve the mixer equations at the outgoing taps to realize each strip. Fix its last h+2 bits. They determine the zero-key suffix, the selected keys and sensors, and their masked readings. Prescribe any leading a-h zero-key output bits and solve the leading mixed bits backwards because the current bit enters alone. Each short transcript extends by every leading word, even if several tails produce it. Allow 60 to 110 minutes.

new.title: Can four sensors and two raw switch flips attain the fixed suffix transcript bound?
new.statement:
∀ d : Nat, d = 1 ∨ d = 2 →
  let mixBit := fun (pulse : Finset Nat) (j : Nat) =>
    xor (decide (j ∈ pulse)) (xor (decide (j+d ∈ pulse)) (decide (j+2*d ∈ pulse)))
  let chi := fun (bit : Nat → Bool) (j : Nat) =>
    xor (bit j) (!(bit (j+1)) && bit (j+2))
  let allowed := fun (p : Finset Nat) => p ⊆ Finset.range (7+2*d) ∧ p.card ≤ 2
  ∃ p M : Finset Nat, allowed p ∧ M ⊆ Finset.range 5 ∧ M.card = 4 ∧ 4 ∈ M ∧ (2 ∉ M ∨ 3 ∉ M) ∧
    ∀ a : Nat, 5 ≤ a →
      let transcript := fun (u : Nat) =>
        let first := (Finset.range a).filter (fun j => chi (fun i => u.testBit i) j = true)
        let bit := fun j : Nat => xor (u.testBit (a-5+j)) (mixBit p j)
        (first, M.filter (fun j => chi bit j = true))
      ((Finset.range (2^(a+2))).image transcript).card = 2^(a-5) * 124
new.unlocks: tests whether sparse fixed probes attain the unrestricted transcript count with a missing sensor
new.context: At five sites try the two masks and up to two switch flips among 7+2d positions. For each zero-key reply set the last two bits freely and solve the rest backwards. Sum distinct masked follow-up replies. A count of 124 certifies one spacing. A negative can exhaust the options at one spacing. Lift to every length by prescribing the leading replies and solving backwards with the seven-bit tail fixed. A smaller-circuit companion cannot exist because the budget counts flipped switches and sensors. Allow 35 to 70 minutes.

new.title: Can one feedback bit identify the strip with four sensors and two raw flips per query?
new.statement:
∀ d : Nat, d = 1 ∨ d = 2 →
  let mixBit := fun (pulse : Finset Nat) (j : Nat) =>
    xor (decide (j ∈ pulse)) (xor (decide (j+d ∈ pulse)) (decide (j+2*d ∈ pulse)))
  let chi := fun (bit : Nat → Bool) (j : Nat) =>
    xor (bit j) (!(bit (j+1)) && bit (j+2))
  let allowed := fun (p : Finset Nat) => p ⊆ Finset.range (7+2*d) ∧ p.card ≤ 2
  ∃ (p0 p1 M : Finset Nat), allowed p0 ∧ allowed p1 ∧ M ⊆ Finset.range 5 ∧ M.card = 4 ∧ 4 ∈ M ∧ (2 ∉ M ∨ 3 ∉ M) ∧
    ∀ a : Nat, 5 ≤ a →
      let transcript := fun (u : Nat) =>
        let b := fun i : Nat => u.testBit i
        let first := (Finset.range a).filter (fun j => chi b j = true)
        let pulse := if chi b (a-1) then p1 else p0
        let bit := fun j : Nat => xor (b (a-5+j)) (mixBit pulse j)
        (first, M.filter (fun j => chi bit j = true))
      ((Finset.range (2^(a+2))).image transcript).card = 2^(a+2)
new.unlocks: tests whether a sparse pulse chosen by one feedback bit can identify every strip with a missing sensor
new.context: Partition the 32 zero-key replies by their last bit. For each allowed mask and pulse test all four tails on each reply of a half. Choose pulses independently with one common mask. To exclude a mask at one spacing give collisions for every pulse on one half. Lift by reconstructing the earlier strip bits from the full zero-key reply and the seven-bit tail. A smaller-circuit companion cannot exist because the budget counts flipped switches and sensors. Allow 35 to 70 minutes.

new.title: Six masks give every pairwise distance after a one-round name reply
new.statement:
∀ h : Nat, 0 < h →
  let bit := fun (u j : Nat) =>
    xor (u.testBit j) (!(u.testBit (j+1)) && u.testBit (j+2))
  let reply := fun u : Nat =>
    ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, if bit u j then 2^j else 0
  let fiber := fun z : Nat =>
    (Finset.range (2^(h+2))).filter (fun u => reply u = z)
  let dist := fun (Q : List (Nat × Nat)) (u v : Nat) =>
    (Q.filter (fun p => bit (u ^^^ p.1) p.2 != bit (v ^^^ p.1) p.2)).length
  let mask := fun (top r : Nat) => ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (r+1), 2^(top-2*i)
  let six := fun (r s : Nat) =>
    let a := mask h r
    let b := 2^(h+1)
    let c := mask (h-1) s
    [a, b, a ^^^ b, b ^^^ c, (a ^^^ b) ^^^ c, a ^^^ c]
  let wt := fun (Q : List (Nat × Nat)) (v : Nat) =>
    (Q.filter (fun p => xor
      (v.testBit (p.2+1) && p.1.testBit (p.2+2))
      (v.testBit (p.2+2) && p.1.testBit (p.2+1)))).length
  let stop := fun (z lane : Nat) =>
    ((List.range ((h-lane)/2)).filter (fun i => z.testBit (h-1-lane-2*i))).headD ((h-lane)/2)
  ∀ z < 2^h, ∀ (Q : List (Nat × Nat)), (∀ p ∈ Q, p.2 < h) → ∀ t : Nat,
    (((fiber z).product (fiber z)).filter
      (fun uv => uv.1 ≠ uv.2 ∧ dist Q uv.1 uv.2 = t)).card =
    2 * ((six (stop z 0) (stop z 1)).filter (fun v => wt Q v == t)).length
new.unlocks: counts collisions and exact Hamming distances on any prescribed follow-up reading list
new.context: Choose the two tail bits freely and invert the quadratic recurrence backwards. Up to a translation the four strips are 0, B+C, A and A+B. B marks the final site. The alternating masks A and C run backwards to their guard stops. Enumerate the six unordered pair differences. The zero-key readings agree, so expanding each shifted comparison leaves the XOR of the two cross terms in the weight. Count repeated list entries and double for ordering. Allow 70 to 130 minutes.

new.title: A weighted cover of guard-stop pairs gives the exact feedback menu budget
new.statement:
∀ h : Nat, 0 < h →
  let bit := fun (u j : Nat) =>
    xor (u.testBit j) (!(u.testBit (j+1)) && u.testBit (j+2))
  let reply := fun u : Nat =>
    ∑ j ∈ Finset.range h, if bit u j then 2^j else 0
  let fiber := fun z : Nat =>
    (Finset.range (2^(h+2))).filter (fun u => reply u = z)
  let dist := fun (Q : List (Nat × Nat)) (u v : Nat) =>
    (Q.filter (fun p => bit (u ^^^ p.1) p.2 != bit (v ^^^ p.1) p.2)).length
  let mask := fun (top r : Nat) => ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (r+1), 2^(top-2*i)
  let six := fun (r s : Nat) =>
    let a := mask h r
    let b := 2^(h+1)
    let c := mask (h-1) s
    [a, b, a ^^^ b, b ^^^ c, (a ^^^ b) ^^^ c, a ^^^ c]
  let wt := fun (Q : List (Nat × Nat)) (v : Nat) =>
    (Q.filter (fun p => xor
      (v.testBit (p.2+1) && p.1.testBit (p.2+2))
      (v.testBit (p.2+2) && p.1.testBit (p.2+1)))).length
  let replies := Finset.range (2^h)
  let m := h/2
  let n := (h-1)/2
  ∀ (menu : Finset (List (Nat × Nat))) (b D target : Nat),
    (∀ Q ∈ menu, ∀ p ∈ Q, p.2 < h) →
    let good := fun (z : Nat) (Q : List (Nat × Nat)) =>
      (((fiber z).product (fiber z)).filter
        (fun uv => uv.1 ≠ uv.2 ∧ dist Q uv.1 uv.2 < D)).card = 0
    (∃ pick : Nat → List (Nat × Nat), replies.image pick ⊆ menu ∧
      (replies.image pick).card ≤ b ∧
      target ≤ (replies.filter (fun z => good z (pick z))).card) ↔
    ∃ bank : Finset (List (Nat × Nat)), bank.Nonempty ∧ bank ⊆ menu ∧ bank.card ≤ b ∧
      target ≤ ∑ r ∈ Finset.range (m+1), ∑ s ∈ Finset.range (n+1),
        if (bank.filter (fun Q => (six r s).all (fun v => decide (D ≤ wt Q v)) = true)).Nonempty
        then 2^(h-(min (r+1) m + min (s+1) n)) else 0
new.unlocks: reduces the choice of a limited feedback menu to weighted coverage on quadratically many guard pairs
new.context: Back-substitute from the two tail bits. The four strips differ by the six listed masks; expanding shifted comparisons gives their weights. A list covers a guard pair precisely when every weight reaches D. A stop fixes min(r+1,m) bits in a lane; the two lanes are disjoint. Sum the multiplicities of covered pairs. The image of any policy is a cover of its successes. Choose a covering list per type, with a default elsewhere. A smaller-circuit companion cannot exist because the budget counts distinct lists. Allow 60 to 120 minutes.

new.sketch: Exploration of one NOT on an eight-vertex graph. Test an AND/OR witness against all 256 inputs, then prove that shorter circuits with at most one NOT fail using a gate lower bound or an exhaustive certificate. For a saving, exhibit the one-NOT circuit and exclude every shorter or equal-sized AND/OR circuit. The graph reader will inspect the shared wires and the input of the NOT in each saving. An equality removes this graph from the search for a saving.

changed.title: A fan-in-two circuit finds whether q parity answers make all selected one-round probes affine and counts the passing keys when they do
changed.statement:
∀ (k m t q : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k),
  let K := ZMod 2
  let W := Fin k → K
  let X := Fin m → K
  let ix := fun pos : ℕ => (⟨pos % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (w : W) (j : Fin k) => w (ix (j.val+k-s%k))
  let mixed := fun (d s : ℕ) (w name : W) =>
    let z := rot s w + name
    fun mid : Fin k => z mid + z (ix (mid.val+d)) + z (ix (mid.val+k-d%k))
  ∀ (site : Fin t → Fin k) (col : Fin t → Bool),
    let spacing := fun spacingId => if col spacingId then 2 else 1
    let start := fun startId => if col startId then 3 else 1
    let injectAt := fun injectId => if col injectId then 4 else 0
    let inputs := (m+5)*k+t
    ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (flag : Fin (inputs+C.size))
      (out : Fin (k+1) → Fin (inputs+C.size)),
      PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack inputs C ∧
      C.size ≤ 2^20*(k+m+t+2)^8*3^(min q (min m t)) ∧
      ∀ (base : W) (gen : Fin m → W) (u v cr cc : W) (wanted : Fin t → K),
        let key := fun x : X => base + ∑ g : Fin m, x g • gen g
        let probe := fun (raw : W) (idx : Fin t) =>
          let y := mixed (spacing idx) (start idx) raw (if col idx then v else u)
          let j := site idx
          y j + (1+y (ix (j.val+1))) * y (ix (j.val+2)) +
            rot (injectAt idx) raw j + (if col idx then cc j else cr j)
        let operand := fun (p : Fin t) (offset : ℕ) (g : Fin m) =>
          mixed (spacing p) (start p) (gen g) 0 (ix ((site p).val+offset))
        let hits := ∃ basis : Fin q → X,
          let D := Submodule.span K (Set.range basis)
          ∀ j, operand j 1 ∈ D ∨ operand j 2 ∈ D ∨ operand j 1 + operand j 2 ∈ D
        let flat := ∃ U : Submodule K X, m ≤ Module.finrank K U + q ∧
          ∀ (z : X) (p : Fin t), ∃ (ell : X →ₗ[K] K) (c : K),
            ∀ x ∈ U, probe (key (z+x)) p = ell x + c
        let pack := fun word : W => List.ofFn (fun bit : Fin k => decide (word bit ≠ 0))
        let bits := pack base ++ (List.ofFn (fun h => pack (gen h))).flatten ++
          pack u ++ pack v ++ pack cr ++ pack cc ++ List.ofFn (fun targetId => decide (wanted targetId ≠ 0))
        (hits ↔ flat) ∧ ((C.wires bits).getD flag.val false = true ↔ hits) ∧
        (hits →
          let count := Nat.card { raw : W // raw ∈ Set.range key ∧ ∀ p, probe raw p = wanted p }
          ∀ o : Fin (k+1), (C.wires bits).getD (out o).val false = count.testBit o.val)
changed.unlocks: Finds shared parity questions and counts a requested key fiber even when its quadratic equations have large span.
changed.context: Restrict the two linear operand forms to a direction space. Their product is affine exactly when one form or their sum vanishes there. Maintain the span of chosen queries. At the first uncovered probe, branch on its two forms and their sum. Each increases rank, and any solution extending the node must contain a choice. Choose one successful basis before doing any counting. On each binary answer cell combine the parity equations with the now affine probes, eliminate, sum the fiber sizes, and divide by the generator kernel size.

let header := fun n : Nat => List.replicate n true ++ [false]
let width := fun n : Nat => n.log2+1
let pack := fun (k : Nat) (rows : List (List Nat)) =>
  header k ++ rows.flatMap (fun row => row.flatMap (bits (width k)))
let well := fun (k : Nat) (rows : List (List Nat)) => ∀ row ∈ rows,
  row.length = 4 ∧ row.Nodup ∧ ∀ v ∈ row, v < k
let wins := fun (k : Nat) (rows : List (List Nat)) (P : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)) =>
  Function.Involutive P ∧ ∀ row ∈ rows, ∃ u : Fin k, u.val ∈ row ∧
    (P u).val ∈ row ∧ P u ≠ u
let lang : Language Bool := {x | ∃ k rows, well k rows ∧ pack k rows = x ∧
  ∃ P : Equiv.Perm (Fin k), wins k rows P}
let witness := fun (k : Nat) (P : Equiv.Perm (Fin k)) =>
  (List.finRange k).flatMap (fun i => bits (width k) (P i).val)
let R : Set (List Bool × List Bool) := {z | ∃ k rows, well k rows ∧ pack k rows = z.1 ∧
  ∃ P : Equiv.Perm (Fin k), wins k rows P ∧ witness k P = z.2}
PEqualNP.Library.NPComplete lang ∧ PEqualNP.Library.PolyTimeReducible PEqualNP.Search.SAT lang ∧
  PEqualNP.Library.DecidableInPolyTime PEqualNP.Library.encodePair R ∧
  (∀ x w, (x,w) ∈ R → w.length ≤ (x.length+1)^2) ∧
  (∀ k rows, well k rows → ∃ E : {P : Equiv.Perm (Fin k) // wins k rows P} ≃
    {w : List Bool // (pack k rows,w) ∈ R}, ∀ P, (E P).val = witness k P.val)
changed.unlocks: Gives the Karp classification of the full binary language and unique accepting certificates for individual winning pairings.
changed.context: Read the header and fixed-width records, checking distinct names and bounds. Read exactly one partner field per vertex. Check range and involution by table lookup. In each row test its six pairs. This recognizes exactly the canonical witnesses and gives membership in NP. Compose the native CNF normalizer with the direct emitter, sending malformed words to the empty nonencoding. The two bijections give the SAT reduction on all strings. Apply checked Cook-Levin and transitivity.

changed.title: Vertex covers encode every affine pair control for optimal fan-in-two AND/OR equality and AND/OR/NOT crown circuits, with a converse for every graph
changed.statement:
let header := fun z : Nat => List.replicate z true ++ [false]
let pairs := fun n : Nat => (List.finRange n).flatMap (fun i =>
  ((List.finRange n).filter (fun j => decide (i < j))).map (fun j => (i,j)))
let fast := fun f : List Bool → List Bool =>
  ∃ M : Turing.TM2ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => x) (fun x : List Bool => x) f,
    ∀ i, Finite (M.tm.Γ i)
∃ write back : List Bool → List Bool, fast write ∧ fast back ∧
  (∀ (k : Nat) (crown : Bool), 2 ≤ k → (crown = true → 7 ≤ k) →
  let nr := if crown then k+2 else k
  let nc := if crown then k+1 else k
  let A := fun (i : Fin nr) (j : Fin nc) => if crown then
    decide (i.val ≠ k+1 ∧ ¬ (i.val < k ∧ i.val = j.val)) else decide (i.val = j.val)
  let Fn := (Fin nr → Bool) → (Fin nc → Bool) → Bool
  let eligible := fun f : Fn => ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    (if crown then PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 2*k+1 else PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size+1 ≤ 2*k) ∧
    PEqualNP.Represents.Represents A C ∧ ∀ x y, f x y = C.eval (List.ofFn x ++ List.ofFn y)
  ∀ (hard : List ((Fin nr → Bool) × (Fin nc → Bool)))
    (soft : List (((Fin nr → Bool) × (Fin nc → Bool)) × Bool)),
  let fits := fun f : Fn => eligible f ∧ ∀ h ∈ hard, f h.1 h.2 = crown
  let score := fun f : Fn => (soft.filter (fun t => decide (f t.1.1 t.1.2 = t.2))).length
  let probe := fun f : Fn => (pairs k).toFinset.filter (fun e =>
    f (fun i => decide (i.val = e.1.val ∨ i.val = e.2.val)) (fun _ => false) = !crown)
  let vs := (pairs k).toFinset
  let strong := fun I : Finset (Fin k × Fin k) => ∀ K ⊆ I,
    ∃ (offset : Int) (w : Fin k × Fin k → Int), ∀ f : Fn, fits f → probe f ∩ I = K →
      (score f : Int) = offset + ((probe f) \ I).sum w
  let active := fun S : Finset (Fin k × Fin k) =>
    ∃ cube : Finset (Fin k × Fin k) → Fn,
      (∀ T ⊆ S, fits (cube T) ∧ probe (cube T) = T) ∧
      S.powerset.sum (fun T => (-1 : Int)^(S.card-T.card)*(score (cube T) : Int)) ≠ 0
  let banks := fun z : (Fin nr → Bool) × (Fin nc → Bool) => List.ofFn z.1 ++ List.ofFn z.2
  let x := [crown] ++ header k ++ header hard.length ++ hard.flatMap banks ++
    header soft.length ++ soft.flatMap (fun t => banks t.1 ++ [t.2])
  ∃ G : (Fin k × Fin k) → (Fin k × Fin k) → Bool,
    write x = (pairs k).flatMap (fun e => (pairs k).map (G e)) ∧
    (∀ e ∈ vs, ∀ f ∈ vs, G e f = true ↔ e ≠ f ∧ ∃ S, e ∈ S ∧ f ∈ S ∧ active S) ∧
    ∀ I ⊆ vs, strong I ↔ ∀ e ∈ vs, ∀ f ∈ vs, G e f = true → e ∈ I ∨ f ∈ I) ∧
  ∀ (v : Nat) (H : Fin v → Fin v → Bool),
    let source := header v ++ (pairs v).map (fun e => H e.1 e.2)
    let k := 2*v+2
    let block := fun (e : Fin k × Fin k) (i : Fin v) => e.1.val = 2*i.val ∧ e.2.val = 2*i.val+1
    let bans := (pairs k).filter (fun e => decide (¬∃ i : Fin v, block e i))
    let edges := (pairs v).filter (fun z => H z.1 z.2)
    let zero := List.replicate k false
    let bword := fun (e : Fin k × Fin k) => (List.finRange k).map (fun i => decide (i=e.1 ∨ i=e.2))
    let row := fun (z : Fin v × Fin v) => (List.finRange k).map
      (fun i => decide (i.val/2=z.1.val ∨ i.val/2=z.2.val))
    back source = [false] ++ header k ++ header bans.length ++
      bans.flatMap (fun e => bword e ++ zero) ++ header edges.length ++
      edges.flatMap (fun z => row z ++ zero ++ [true]) ∧
    write (back source) = (pairs k).flatMap (fun e => (pairs k).map (fun f =>
      decide (∃ i j : Fin v, block e i ∧ block f j ∧ i ≠ j ∧ H (min i j) (max i j) = true)))
changed.unlocks: Identifies the minimum number of fixed pair probes with the minimum vertex-cover size for arbitrary labeled observations. All graphs are realized on disjoint probes.
changed.context: Use the signed coefficient criterion on the graph allowed by hard samples. A term containing two uncontrolled probes survives in some branch by inversion over the fixed probes. Ask for a nonzero matching extension containing each disjoint pair of probes to write all adjacencies. Contradictory hard data give an empty conflict graph. In reverse allocate a disjoint name pair per source vertex, ban every other transposition, and reward the union of two blocks for each source edge. Exactly these two-probe interactions survive.

changed.title: Copying essential inputs into disjoint OR blocks costs exactly one shared gate per extra input at every NOT budget
changed.statement:
∀ (n m q b : Nat) (π : Fin m → Fin n) (F : Fin q → (Fin n → Bool) → Bool),
  Function.Surjective π →
  (∀ j, ∃ x y, F j x ≠ F j y) →
  (∀ i : Fin n, ∃ (j : Fin q) (x y : Fin n → Bool), (∀ u, u ≠ i → x u = y u) ∧ F j x ≠ F j y) →
  let expand := fun (y : Fin m → Bool) (i : Fin n) => decide (∃ u, π u = i ∧ y u = true)
  let fits := fun (k : Nat) (T : Fin q → (Fin k → Bool) → Bool) (s : Nat) =>
    ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (tap : Fin q → Nat),
      PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ s ∧
      PEqualNP.NotBracket.notCount C ≤ b ∧
      ∀ j x, (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (tap j) false = T j x
  let lifted := fun j y => F j (expand y)
  (∀ s, fits m lifted s → m-n ≤ s) ∧
  ∀ s, fits n F s ↔ fits m lifted (s+(m-n))
changed.unlocks: A finite shared witness covers every independent OR expansion with an exact gate budget at each NOT allowance.
changed.context: Build each block OR once and share it. Discard ignored NOT operands and treat missing or forward reads as false. Fix one redundant copy to zero. It affects an output but cannot itself be an output wire, by symmetry with its sibling. Its first effective gate becomes constant or a copy. Propagate constants, bypass copies and renumber survivors. All restricted outputs stay nonconstant, so no new constant gate is needed. Repeat down to one input per block. The NOT count never increases.
